test-case.name: TheMachinesScenariosOwnLoadoutCanDoTheWholeColdDemoItsTextPromises
test-case.output: [Scenario] [Machines] You start on wild ground with a proofing trough, a hearth and a still, two flasks of bog-mire and three empty ones, garments, a reagent for each element, a sounding rod and the parts Cinderhold's pump asks for. [Scenario] [Machines] 1. Open the pack, pick the hearth and choose 'set down' east, then the still west ('make camp here' lays out every kit at once). 2. Press C toward the hearth: highlight 'stoke' and read what it does, then choose it. 3. Press C toward the still: it shows your mix status and, beside the lit fire, offers 'bake 12 mire to 1 fire clay' for each of the two mire flasks (each uses 8 mire and 10 fuel; settle some mire instead to compare). [Scenario] [Machines] 3b. A steam vent steams six cells east of you. Pick up the still you set down in step 1 (or use a fresh kit), walk three cells east and set it down east (it lands two cells from the vent: the cell right beside a vent is refused), then press C toward it: settling needs no fire there, and the row says the vent's heat pays. Baking clay still wants the hearth. Examine the vent with mire or the still in your pack for what it is good for. [Scenario] [Machines] 4. Proofing, the short way (no machine): open the pack, choose a reagent (frost lichen, fire moss, spark root or sourmantle fold) and 'press into a flask': the flask then holds that element's proofing, one unit a coat (a stronger reagent makes more coats). Choose the flask, then 'coat <garment>': +35 of that resistance for 100 worn turns, paused when the garment is off; another coat of the same adds turns, another element replaces. Examine the flask and the garment to read it. Wear the cloak, coat it with cold and put a freeze on yourself (a frost vent, an ice lance) to feel the status shorten as well as the damage (drink a frost tonic for a freeze, a lightning tonic for a shock; the steam vent six east scalds for heat). 4a. Proofing for good: set down the trough, press 4 units of one element into a flask, and with 2 fire clay choose 'proof <garment> against <element> for good' at the trough: +25, never wears out, one a garment. Cold from the cloak (+50), a coat (+35) and the trough (+25) is past 100: immune. Bake more clay at the still (4b below). 4b. Pour one of the mire flasks onto your lit hearth (pack, the flask, 'pour ... east'): the row says what it would do. A full flask puts the fire out and the hearth keeps its fuel; stoke and light it again from a flame. [Scenario] [Machines] 4c. The fish trap needs a pool of falling water to fish; a small one has been dug four cells west of you. Walk two cells west, open the pack and choose the trap's 'set down' west: it lands on the shore beside the water, and it offers no cell where there is no fishable water. The reader says when the next fish is due; rest half a day, then 'take the fish'. A second trap on the same pool shares its supply. [Scenario] [Machines] 4d. The shade awning answers the Beating's glare: in the Height hours, ten bareheaded turns on the open pan parch you a stack. Set it down on open ground in the Beating (the south of the world map) and stand under it or in the ring of cells around it: the count resets, as under a roof or a hat. Take it up and the shade goes with it. [Scenario] [Machines] 5. Cinderhold's mine pump: travel to Cinderhold (Overworld.6.6.0, north-west on the world map), find the pump beside the well, press C: its menu shows what each repair needs against what you carry; 'mend for good' uses the two iron spikes, the oak haft and the binding. The pump then reads 'running'. [Scenario] [Machines] 6. The sounding rod works only in an ordinary deep cave: take any stairs down, step in, open the pack, choose 'sound the ground'. It names open ground, a way through and dense stone you have not seen, as a bearing and a distance, and the strike is loud.

test-case.name: EveryElementHasAHazardTheSettlingTrayCanCatchFrom_SoTheWorkshopShowsAllFourCatches
test-case.output: [Scenario] [Workshop] You start on wild ground with every proofing machine and reagent, flasks, fire clay, ten full sets of armor (open the pack), status tonics and the four elemental spell books. A proving post stands beside you; heat hazards lie north-east, cold north-west, acid south-east, shock south-west. [Scenario] [Workshop] 1. Press reagents into flasks: choose a reagent in the pack, 'press into a flask'. Frost lichen, glacier salt and chillcress make cold; fire moss, ember fruit and pitchpod make heat; spark root and prismreed make shock; sourmantle makes acid; glimmer brine makes shock or acid. 2. Coat: choose a flask of proofing, 'coat <garment>' (+35 for 100 worn turns; works on a stack of identical armor, one unit at a time). 3. For good: set down the proofing trough (pack, 'set down'), put 4 units of one element in your flasks, and 'proof <garment> against <element> for good' (4 units and 2 fire clay for +25; one lasting proofing a garment). 4. Make more clay: set down the hearth and still, stoke the fire and bake the four mire flasks (8 mire and 10 fuel per clay), or plant the seeds for more reagents. 4b. Catch reagent from the hazards for nothing: carry a settling tray to any hazard (a steam vent, ash bed, frost vent, ice sheet, or a pool of brine, acid or mire) and press C on the tray kit in your pack: its set-down rows say what each cell would catch (the cell beside a hazard is refused, and so is the cell in line beyond an ash bed or frost vent, which warm and chill what they touch; a cell a little off the line works). It settles one level-one reagent of that hazard's element every half day (four at most, from the hazard's own supply, which refills a day at a time). Rest a few hours, press C beside it, 'gather'; the catch cannot be sold. [Scenario] [Workshop] 5. Test: wear a set (open the pack, equip each piece). Press C beside the proving post: call a Marlback cindercaller or charred husk (heat), ice wight or rune cultist (cold), Marlback stormbinder or vault sentinel (shock), Marlback soursprayer or cave slime (acid); 'send away' removes what it called; 'mend yourself' restores health and clears statuses (a coat stays). Walk the hazards: steam vents, ash beds and fire traps for heat; frost vents, ice and frost runes for cold; acid pools and bog mire for acid; brine for shock (zap yourself with a lightning tonic, or cast an arc bolt, while standing in it). Drink a frost or lightning tonic to put a status on yourself. Your resistance is on the inventory screen's status panel.

test-case.output: [Scenario] [Workshop] You start on wild ground with every proofing machine and reagent, flasks, fire clay, ten full sets of armor (open the pack), status tonics and the four elemental spell books. A proving post stands beside you; heat hazards lie north-east, cold north-west, acid south-east, shock south-west. [Scenario] [Workshop] 1. Press reagents into flasks: choose a reagent in the pack, 'press into a flask'. Frost lichen, glacier salt and chillcress make cold; fire moss, ember fruit and pitchpod make heat; spark root and prismreed make shock; sourmantle makes acid; glimmer brine makes shock or acid. 2. Coat: choose a flask of proofing, 'coat <garment>' (+35 for 100 worn turns; works on a stack of identical armor, one unit at a time). 3. For good: set down the proofing trough (pack, 'set down'), put 4 units of one element in your flasks, and 'proof <garment> against <element> for good' (4 units and 2 fire clay for +25; one lasting proofing a garment). 4. Make more clay: set down the hearth and still, stoke the fire and bake the four mire flasks (8 mire and 10 fuel per clay), or plant the seeds for more reagents. 4b. Catch reagent from the hazards for nothing: carry a settling tray to any hazard (a steam vent, ash bed, frost vent, ice sheet, or a pool of brine, acid or mire) and press C on the tray kit in your pack: its set-down rows say what each cell would catch (the cell beside a hazard is refused, and so is the cell in line beyond an ash bed or frost vent, which warm and chill what they touch; a cell a little off the line works). It settles one level-one reagent of that hazard's element every half day (four at most, from the hazard's own supply, which refills a day at a time). Rest a few hours, press C beside it, 'gather'; the catch cannot be sold. [Scenario] [Workshop] 5. Test: wear a set (open the pack, equip each piece). Press C beside the proving post: call a Marlback cindercaller or charred husk (heat), ice wight or rune cultist (cold), Marlback stormbinder or vault sentinel (shock), Marlback soursprayer or cave slime (acid); 'send away' removes what it called; 'mend yourself' restores health and clears statuses (a coat stays). Walk the hazards: steam vents, ash beds and fire traps for heat; frost vents, ice and frost runes for cold; acid pools and bog mire for acid; brine for shock (zap yourself with a lightning tonic, or cast an arc bolt, while standing in it).
